info.title: About blood-helper
info.subtitle: An intelligent platform for blood bank management and predictive analytics
info.overviewText: blood-helper is a production-grade platform that combines real-time inventory monitoring, machine learning forecasting, and donation campaign management to help hospitals maintain safe blood supply levels.
features: Real-time blood inventory monitoring with critical alert WebSocket push
Per-hospital, per-blood-type consumption forecasting (daily / weekly / monthly)
PSI — Pressure Supply Index: stress-scenario supply sufficiency metric
Wastage analysis with cost estimation by blood type and reason
Donation campaign lifecycle: create → activate → track → complete

mlModels.name: Prophet
mlModels.description: Time-series forecasting model developed by Meta. Handles seasonality, holidays, and trend changepoints. Used for daily/weekly/monthly blood consumption prediction.

mlModels.name: XGBoost
mlModels.description: Gradient-boosted decision trees for tabular data. Used as an ensemble alternative for departments with irregular or sparse consumption history.

mlModels.name: Scikit-Learn
mlModels.description: Provides preprocessing pipelines, feature engineering, and fallback linear regression models. Used to generate training data splits and evaluation metrics.

info.psiDescription: The PSI is a dimensionless sufficiency ratio computed per blood type per hospital:
info.psiFormula: PSI = (Net Valid Stock + Expected Net Inflows) / Expected Demand

psiComponents.label: Net Valid Stock
psiComponents.value: Units that will NOT expire within the forecast horizon, minus reserved units

psiComponents.label: Expected Demand
psiComponents.value: Statistical percentile of daily consumption history × horizon days (Static or EWMA-weighted)

psiComponents.label: Expected Net Inflows
psiComponents.value: Median of historical inflows × horizon × (1 − friction δ), capped conservatively

psiComponents.label: Static method
psiComponents.value: Full history percentile (stable, ignores recent trends)

psiComponents.label: EWMA method
psiComponents.value: Exponentially-weighted moving average — more sensitive to recent demand shifts
